stem: In school-aged children, what is the most common bacterial cause of pneumonia?
explanation: Mycoplasma pneumoniae is the most common bacterial cause of pneumonia in school-aged children.

optionExplanations.A: Incorrect because Streptococcus pneumoniae is an important cause of community-acquired pneumonia, but it is not the most common bacterial cause in school-aged children.
optionExplanations.B: Correct because Mycoplasma pneumoniae is the most frequent bacterial cause of pneumonia in school-aged children and is a classic cause of atypical pneumonia.
optionExplanations.C: Incorrect because Staphylococcus aureus can cause severe pneumonia, but it is less common than Mycoplasma pneumoniae in this age group.
optionExplanations.D: Incorrect because Haemophilus influenzae can cause respiratory infection, but it is not the leading bacterial cause of pneumonia in school-aged children.
optionExplanations.E: Incorrect because Chlamydia pneumoniae can cause atypical pneumonia, but Mycoplasma pneumoniae is more common in school-aged children.

source.hint: Identify the bacterium that is particularly prevalent in children who have reached school age.
